newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: No forward cover burden for Sappi in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: No forward cover burden for Sappi in 96/97.

text.p: South African paper and pulp producer Sappi Ltd said on Tuesday export earnings in the new financial year would be boosted by a weak rand as all forward cover taken on the rand in the past year had been cleared.

"The adverse effect of the decision to cover one third of the group's southern African export sales before the collapse of prices is now behind us," managing director Eugene van As said at the presentation of Sappi's year end results.
"(We) will benefit substantially from the weaker rand in the new year," he said, adding that the group was also expected to benefit from an improvement in world pulp and paper prices.
Financial director Bill Hewitt told Reuters the losses on forward exchange positions amounted to around 200 million rand.
"We have not worked it out exactly, but it is around 200 million rand," Hewitt said.
He said some 50 million rand of the cover had not been used by the September 30 year-end and this amount had been written off so as to start the new year with a clean slate.
"We don't want to adulterate the new year, last year was bad enough," Hewitt said.
South Africa's rand has weakened almost 30 percent against the U.S. dollar this year. The rand was trading at 4.6350 at 1010 GMT.
Sappi on Tuesday reported year earnings plunged 73 percent to 230 cents a share from 846 cents previously, below an expected consensus of 266.6 cents.
It blamed the weak earnings result on soft world pulp and paper demand and prices.
Van As said both the demand and prices for paper products were on an upward trend, pointing to an improvement in Sappi's earnings in the 1996/97 year.
"In 1997 we see a year of rising prices (in the U.S.). If it is anywhere near where German and European prices have been going, 1997 is going to be much better than 1996," van As said.
"We think the demand for paper is becoming strong...In the short term everyone is building inventory, especially publishers."
Sappi shares slid almost three percent on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange following the results release. At 1010GMT they were trading 2.8 percent weaker at 40.80 -- a slide of 120 cents.
